newsitem.title: USA: White House's Bowles makes budget top priority.
newsitem.headline: White House's Bowles makes budget top priority.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff designate Erskine Bowles intends to make balancing the federal budget his top priority, a group of moderate House Republicans said Thursday after their initial meeting with President Clinton's new top aide.

Leaders of the moderate group, known as the Tuesday Lunch Bunch, said they came away from the meeting with the impression that Bowles would take more conservative positions on economic issues which affect financial markets than had his predecessor, Leon Panetta.

Rep. Mike Castle of Delaware, one of the co-chairs of the moderate group, said Bowles told them balancing the budget was the chief reason he agreed to leave his business in North Carolina and take the White House position. "That is why he personally came back," Castle said.

Castle and others viewed the White House request for an early meeting as an attempt to open lines of communication with moderate Republicans. Castle and co-chairs Nancy Johnson of Connecticut and Fred Upton of Michigan rejected the idea that the White House was attempting to drive a wedge in the Republican party, but rather was looking for areas of agreement.
Rep. Mark Foley, R-Florida, described the meeting as a chance to get to know each other and felt the Republican budget group and Bowles were both working to moderate the extremes of their parties.
"We had a very good dialogue. I think this sets the stage for real bipartisan cooperation," Upton added.
Other key issues Bowles outlined for the group were overhaul of the Superfund toxic waste clean up laws, campaign finance reform, education and juvenile justice programs.

As Upton and other moderates described their impression of Bowles' value in negotiations with the Republican-controlled Congress, "He doesn't have any 'political baggage'... (Leon Panetta) was a political animal. Erskine is not."
"He is looking to establish a level of trust," Upton added.
The White House had requested the meeting with the moderates and the next session with the administration in early January will be with Office of Management and Budget director Franklin Raines.
